title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
text: Page 2 of 64 In an effort to enhance passenger safety and safeguard equipment, Indian Railways has adopted fire and smoke detection system, along with fire detection and suppression system, for its coaches. These technologies represent a significant advancement in train safety, addressing a critical need for prompt and reliable detection and suppression of potential fire hazards. By incorporating these advanced fire safety technologies, Indian Railways is taking a proactive stance on ensuring the safety and well-being of the passengers traveling in its network. This forward-looking approach not only boosts passenger confidence but also contributes to a safer, more secure rail travel experience across the nation. The Railway Board has advised IRCAMTECH to develop a maintenance schedule, troubleshooting guidelines, and material requirements to streamline the maintenance of fire and smoke detection system and fire detection and suppression system. As advised, IRCAMTECH has prepared the maintenance manual for the fire and smoke detection system and fire detection and suppression system.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
text: Page 3 of 64 Page 4 of 64 The safety and well-being of passengers traveling on the Indian Railways are of paramount importance, especially in air-conditioned coaches where fire hazards can pose significant risks. To address these concerns, Indian Railways has implemented fire and smoke detection systems alongside fire detection and suppression systems. These technologies are designed to ensure early identification of potential fire threats, enabling prompt alerts and rapid response to mitigate risks. By incorporating sensitive smoke and heat detectors, along with automatic suppression capabilities, these systems significantly enhance passenger safety, minimize equipment damage, and ensure compliance with stringent safety regulations. The integration of such advanced systems not only fosters a safer travel environment but also reinforces Indian Railways' commitment to maintaining high standards of operational safety and passenger protection. On advice of the Railway Board IRCAMTECH has prepared the maintenance manual for the fire and smoke detection system and fire detection and suppression system.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
text: The Fire and Smoke Detection System (FSDS) is a critical safety feature designed to detect and alert the presence of fire and smoke within the Air-Conditioned coach. Below mentioned are the key details of the system: I. Design: The FSDS is designed for very early warning for smoke/fire incidents in air-conditioned coaches. II. Sampling Nozzles and Pipe Network: These include Sampling Nozzles, capillary tubes and PVC pipeline strategically placed throughout the coaches to collect air samples to analyze the existence of fire/ smoke. III. Control Panel / Fire Detection Panel and Power Panel: This panel, available in each coach, contains the Aspirating Smoke Detection Unit and Power panel for 24V battery backup and DC-DC Convertor to convert 110VDC to 24VDC. The Aspiration smoke detection Unit collects air samples from throughout the coach, analyses in the detection panel for existence of fire/smoke and initiates appropriate responses. IV. Alarms: Audible and visual alarms alert passengers and train staff to the presence of smoke or fire, enabling swift evacuation and response. V.

Automatic Response: The FSDS has provision of integration with the train's braking system to automatically stop the train in case of a fire emergency.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
text: It is an advanced safety system designed to detect the presence of fire/smoke and automatically suppress it to prevent the spread and minimize damage. I. Detection: The system uses point type smoke detectors, point type heat detectors and linear heat detection cable placed suitably inside the coach. II. Alarm: a) When the smoke is detected through smoke detector, it will raise pre- alarm in detection panel. b) When the heat/fire is detected through heat detector, it will raise fire- alarm in detection panel. c) When the heat/fire is detected through LHD cable, it will raise fire- alarm in detection panel.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
text: Suppression: The Power Cars / Pantry coaches are equipped with a High Pressure Water Mist Fire Suppression System. In case of a fire, alarm raised by detection unit, the system is designed to suppress the fire and prevent it from spreading. Page 8 of 64

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
text: 4.1.1. An Aspiration Type Automatic Smoke / Fire Detection with Alarm System gives early warning against any smoke/fire. In this system, Sampling pipe/ Sampling points network is designed to cover entire coach’s passenger area including lavatories, doorway & gangway of coach. A system of intake pipes with defined sampling orifices performs active air sampling and sends the smoke levels to the Central Control Unit (CCU).

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
text: Air is drawn into the pipe network through the sampling points (Aspiration System) from a close surrounding and traverses to a very sensitive smoke detector consisting of an aspirator, detection chamber, dual stage filter and necessary networking card. The negative pressure of an aspirator helps in drawing ambient air to a detection chamber where scattering of light occurs and detection of smoke takes place. FSDS system works on the principle of actively drawing air samples from the coach through sampling points and directed to a detection chamber in the detector. The presence of smoke in the sample air results in the scattering of the laser that is instantly detected by a configuration of light receiver. Depending upon the smoke level, an output signal is processed and displayed on the detector chamber. The system is designed as a multi-level alarm system with each level of smoke threshold resulting in a different alarm warning for the passengers. VESDA Module Page 10 of 64

text: VESDA Module Page 10 of 64 Indication of alarms shall be as under: a) System for Complete Rake: ● Alert: Flasher light to be activated at CMS, no indication to the passengers in the affected coach ● Action: Flasher light to be activated on fire detection panel of affected coach ● Fire: Brake application shall take place automatically. After a time, delay of 55 seconds after activation of brake application, an audio visual alarm like a hooter or buzzer etc. along with flashing lights should be activated in affected coach. Audio visual (Hooter & Flasher Light) indication to be continued at CMS b) System for Stand-alone Coach: ● Alert: LED to flash on fire detection panel, no indication to the passengers in the affected coach ● Action: Flasher light to be activated on fire detection panel of affected coach ● Fire: Brake application shall take place automatically. After a time, delay of 55 seconds after activation of brake application, an audio visual alarm like a hooter or buzzer etc. along with flashing lights should be activated in affected coach. title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
text: In all possible conditions of the coach environment, the system shall respond within 60 seconds after the cessation of energization. 1. The airflow through the aspirating smoke detection unit shall be monitored to detect leakage or obstruction on the sampling device or sampling point(s). 1. Aspirating Smoke Detection Unit - The aspirating smoke detection unit under test is set up in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. 2. Anemometer- To measure the normal airflow value (Fn) by a calibrated flow meter such as an anemometer with the worst-case sampling device. The minimum distance between the anemometer and the first sampling point is 30 cm. No sampling point shall be made between the aspirating smoke detection unit and the anemometer. Page 26 of 64 First Sampling Point Aspirating Smoke Detection Unit

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
text: 1. The normal airflow (Fn)(Lt./min.) shall be determined from the sampling configuration used for the fire test with the help of application software or anemometer 2. The aspirating smoke detection unit under test shall be tested at the test flow rate (Ft) (i.e. Ft = Fn ± 10%) for testing the airflow monitoring. 3. For an aspirating smoke detection unit under test that has a memorized normal flow, The Fn shall be entered to the memory in accordance with normal operating instruction for the detection system. This shall only be done once at the start of each test and shall not be done during/after the conditioning. 4. For decreased flow, the volumetric airflow is decreased from Fn by 20%, which shall be observed through application software or anemometer installed between the sampling pipe and aspirating smoke detection unit 5. For increased flow the volumetric airflow is increased from Fn by 20%, which shall be observed through application software or anemometer installed between the sampling pipe and detection system unit.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
text: 1. When the volumetric air flow reading in the system reaches the value of Fn - 20%. the aspirating smoke detection unit shall generate an airflow fault signal. 2. When the volumetric air flow reading in the system reaches the value of Fn + 20%, the aspirating smoke detection unit shall generate an airflow fault signal.

text: 1. Provision of Common interface/screen for status monitoring & data downloading having provision for various indications. Schematic of the same is as under: 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. 7. 8. The size of common interface panel should be within 300X250 for indications & data download panel. Indicators should be 22mm Panel mounted LED indicators (pilot light) and USB port should be covered with protective cover to avoid ingress of dust. 2. Provision of mechanical clamp for isolating cock and proximity/limit sensor (or any other suitable mechanism) to prevent isolation of brake valve & in cases of isolation, to capture and display on common interface/screen. 3. Lithium-ion battery having higher back-up i.e. in range of 10-12 hrs with inbuilt safety measures adopted globally including fire safety measures. 4. Modified audio message and all other works required for upgradation of FSDS system as specified in Amendment-1 of spec no. RDSO/2008/CG- 04(Rev-06) or latest RDSO specification. 5. Common interface/screen panel along with associated accessories for system operation shall be EN 50155 compliant. 6. All software, hardwares etc.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
text: 5. Common interface/screen panel along with associated accessories for system operation shall be EN 50155 compliant. 6. All software, hardwares etc. and any other material required to make the system fully functional without any constraints and for regular maintenance. 7. Cables used in the system shall be fire survival cables according to EN 50200.Survival duration classification of PH30 (30min) or higher is desirable. 8. Power supply of 110 V DC is available. title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
text: 5.1.1. The System is known as Fire Detection and Suppression System (FDSS), it is an integration of two systems one is Fire detection and another one is Fire suppression / extinguishing system. The Fire Detection System consists of Fire and Smoke Detectors placed suitably inside the Generator area/pantry area. The Detectors are connected in a redundant loop to the control module. The Control module is connected to an Audio-Visual Sounder beacon for Alarm in case of a fire. The Fire Suppression System works on the Principle of High Pressure Water Mist System

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
section: Principle of High Pressure Water Mist System
text: The most important effects of fire fighting with water mist are the cooling and oxygen displacement effect. Through the atomization of water under high pressure, the reaction surface available for the cooling process is significantly enlarged in comparison to conventional low pressure systems. The water mist generated has a total surface area, at least 100 times greater than a conventional sprinkler. The FDSS consists of water cylinders and a nitrogen cylinder, which are the source of the pressurized water mist system. FDSS System has Heat Detectors and Smoke Detectors. Smoke Detectors will provide pre-alarm, and after pre-alarm, manual activation of the system is done through an activation switch provided on the control panel. Heat Detector provides fire alarm as well as automatic actuation of Fire Suppression System. On receiving the Fire Alarm (through Heat Detectors/LHD Cable), an automatic fire suppression system is operated. Fire detection unit constantly monitors and controls the fire protection system and is also protected by a UPS with battery backup. The Control unit displays the ready status, relevant faults and alarms.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
section: Principle of High Pressure Water Mist System
text: The Control unit displays the ready status, relevant faults and alarms. The water mist system is activated by an electrically operated solenoid valve/magnetic valve on the nitrogen cylinder. If a fire is detected, a message is sent accordingly to the fire detection evaluation unit and the generator cars vehicle control system, after which ventilation is shut down and the fuel supply to the engines cut off. Visual and acoustic alarms are activated in the guards’ compartment. Page 41 of 64

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
section: Procedure for Testing and Checking of Magnetic Valve
text: 5.1.2. Magnetic Valve The activation procedure is to be simulated as part of inspection. Every magnetic valve is to be activated once, and checked mechanically. The procedure is as follows: 1. Remove the solenoids from the gas valves belonging to the nitrogen cylinders. 2. Apply voltage to the system. 3. Check whether the solenoids are producing magnetic fields, there should not be any magnetic field yet. This can be checked using a metallic object, by inserting it inside the coil (e.g. a screw driver). 4. Check the pressure in the nitrogen cylinders using the manometer fitted. Log the pressure and the position of the area valves. 5. Simulate detection. 6. The processes defined in the system should take place automatically: a)  Alarm signal produced. b)   Check manual activation using the lever c)   Disconnect the connection line. d)   Close the valve outlet using the lock nut 7. Reset the fire alarm system. 8. Next, perform a mechanical inspection of the magnetic valve (to do this put back the solenoid): To perform a mechanical function test, a conventional Allen key as well as a lock nut with vent hole is required. a.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
section: Procedure for Testing and Checking of Magnetic Valve
text: a. Activate the valve electronically for two to three seconds, then switch off the current or deactivate manual activation. b. Undo the vent screw using the Allen key, turning it through half a rotation, which will vent the valve area involved, causing the valve to close audibly. The pressure, however, will remain in the valve outlet. c. By carefully undoing the lock nut by about half a turn, then vent the valve outlet. A short, audible emission of gas signals that the valve has opened correctly as a result of electrical or manual activation. This escape of gas, however, Page 49 of 64 should cease immediately, otherwise the valve has not closed properly. If that happens, do not remove the lock nut. d. If the valve does not close, then it must be replaced. To do this, empty the container through the valve outlet by turning the lock nut by no more than half a turn. Secure the container appropriately before emptying. e. If the valve is working properly, then screw up the vent screw again so that it seals. f. Return the system to its functional state.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
text: A. Coaches: ● All protective equipment such as fuses, contactors, MCBs etc. should be intact and with proper rating. No bypassing and paralleling to be done ● Fire extinguishers as per guidelines with proper validity to be provided. ● Fire detection and alarm system provided in the coaches must be in working condition ● Thermal scanning of Power panels of all coaches on load to done as per extant guideline ● FDSS (Fire Detection and Suppression System) provided in pantry cars should be in working condition and magnet valve for operating the suppression. ● FSDS (Fire Smoke Detection System) should be in working condition. The angle cock connecting the penalty brake application should not be in isolated condition. ● WSP should be in working order. ● Only metal (preferably stainless-steel) dustbins should be provided in coaches. ● Garbage evacuation to be ensured at designated stations. ● Escorting staff should be properly trained and counseled for handling fire incidents. ● Cleaning of LHB ACP panels B. Pantry / Power Cars: ● FDSS (Fire Detection and Suppression System) provided in Power Cars/Pantry Car should be in working condition.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
text: Pantry / Power Cars: ● FDSS (Fire Detection and Suppression System) provided in Power Cars/Pantry Car should be in working condition. ● Leakage/Seepage of Lube and fuel oil in the engine room should be arrested before putting in service. ● All safety equipment including sensors should be in working condition ● Radiator as well as side body filters to be cleaned properly. ● Thermal scanning of power panels of Power Cars on load to done as per extant guideline. ● Escorting staff should be counseled and trained ● Engine room and panel room should be dry.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
text: ● After discharge, allow for appropriate holding time before ventilating the hazard space. ● Always have backup portable fire extinguishers on hand for use in the unlikely event of fire re-ignition. ● Ventilate the hazard area thoroughly by forced ventilation or by opening doors and windows. ● Inspect that all fires have been extinguished and that there are no localized hot spots or other sources of re-ignition present. Page 56 of 64 Caution: ● Ensure the fire is completely extinguished before ventilating the hazard space. ● Ventilate thoroughly or use a self-contained breathing apparatus before entering. ● For areas with sensitive electronic equipment, recovery activities should begin immediately after system discharge and the area is secured from fire re- ignition. This will help protect electronic assets from possible damage.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-2 (LHB & ICF Coaches)
text: jointly with OEM as per the condition of the system. ● Use appropriate PPEs. ● Follow the prescribed inspection, maintenance and testing schedule for the system. ● Proper record keeping of the system. ● Check the indication LEDs in the control/detection panel. ● Ensure that smoke is detected by the aspiration sampling point when it is cleared of blockage due to vandalism or dust/dirt accumulation. ● Ensure that no smoke/fire source is present in the coach if an alarm/alert indication is observed.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-1 (Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat Coaches)
text: Page 2 of 87 In an effort to enhance passenger safety and safeguard equipment, Indian Railways has adopted fire and smoke detection system, along with fire detection and suppression system, for its coaches. These technologies represent a significant advancement in train safety, addressing a critical need for prompt and reliable detection and suppression of potential fire hazards. By incorporating these advanced fire safety technologies, Indian Railways is taking a proactive stance on ensuring the safety and well-being of the passengers traveling in its network. This forward-looking approach not only boosts passenger confidence but also contributes to a safer, more secure rail travel experience across the nation. The Railway Board has advised IRCAMTECH to develop a maintenance schedule, troubleshooting guidelines, and material requirements to streamline the maintenance of fire and smoke detection system and fire detection and suppression system. As advised, IRCAMTECH has prepared the maintenance manual for the fire and smoke detection system and fire detection and suppression system.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-1 (Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat Coaches)
text: Page 3 of 87 Page 4 of 87 The safety and well-being of passengers traveling on the Indian Railways are of paramount importance, especially in air-conditioned coaches where fire hazards can pose significant risks. To address these concerns, Indian Railways has implemented fire and smoke detection systems alongside fire detection and suppression systems. These technologies are designed to ensure early identification of potential fire threats, enabling prompt alerts and rapid response to mitigate risks. By incorporating sensitive smoke and heat detectors, along with automatic suppression capabilities, these systems significantly enhance passenger safety, minimize equipment damage, and ensure compliance with stringent safety regulations. The integration of such advanced systems not only fosters a safer travel environment but also reinforces Indian Railways' commitment to maintaining high standards of operational safety and passenger protection. On the advice of the Railway Board IRCAMTECH has prepared the maintenance manual for the fire and smoke detection system and fire detection and suppression system.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-1 (Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat Coaches)
text: The Fire and Smoke Detection System (FSDS) is a critical safety feature designed to detect and alert the presence of fire and smoke within the Vande Bharat Chaircar Coaches. Below mentioned are the key details of the system: I. Design: The FSDS is designed for very early warning for smoke/ fire incidents in air-conditioned coaches. II. Sampling Nozzles and Pipe Network: These include sampling nozzles, capillary tubes, and pipelines. They are strategically placed throughout the coach to identify signs of fire or smoke by collecting air samples. III. Detection Sensors: These include point-type smoke detectors strategically placed in the coach to identify signs of fire or smoke. IV.Control Panel / Detection Panel: This panel is available in each coach and it contains the Aspirating Smoke Detection Unit and the Fire Panel. The Aspirating Smoke Detection Unit is a sophisticated air sampling smoke detection system designed to provide early warning of fire. The Fire Panel processes signals from the Detection Sensors & Aspirating Smoke Detection Unit and initiates appropriate responses. V.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-1 (Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat Coaches)
text: The Fire Panel processes signals from the Detection Sensors & Aspirating Smoke Detection Unit and initiates appropriate responses. V. Alarms: Audible and visual alarms alert passengers and train staff to the presence of smoke or fire, enabling swift evacuation and response. VI. Automatic Response: The FSDS has provision of integration with the train's braking system to automatically stop the train in case of a fire emergency.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-1 (Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat Coaches)
text: An Aspiration Type Automatic Smoke / Fire Detection with Alarm System is used in the active fire protection of Vande Bharat Coaches. This system consists of a high- sensitivity Aspirating Smoke Detection Unit connected to a network of pipes. These pipes draw air from various points throughout the coach. The sampling chamber in the Aspirating Smoke Detection Unit detects smoke particles suspended in the air before they become visible to the naked eye. In this way, it provides a very early warning of fire events, allowing timely intervention. 1 3 2 4 5 6

text: 4.1.1.1. I. Aspirating Smoke Detection Unit (HOCHIKI – FIRELINK 25): This is a sophisticated air sampling smoke detection system designed to provide early warning of fire. Its key features are:  Air Sampling Technology: It uses sampling pipes to continuously draw air from the protected area into the detector, providing highly sensitive and accurate smoke detection. Page 14 of 87  Laser-Based Detection: Utilizes advanced laser technology to detect the presence of smoke particles in the air samples, enabling early detection of even small amounts of smoke.  Multiple Alarm Levels: Configurable alarm thresholds allow for multiple levels of alarm sensitivity, providing graded alerts depending on the concentration of smoke detected. Threshold Values of the System for Automatic Smoke / Fire Detection System in Vande Bharat Chaicar Coaches (Ver. 2.0) Note: The audio and visual alarm indication at the driver console/desk will be only for Stage-1 (Action) and Stage-2 (Fire) detection.  High Sensitivity: Designed to detect smoke at a very early stage, often before it is visible, allowing for rapid response to potential fire threats.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-1 (Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat Coaches)
text: The Aspiration Type Automatic Smoke/Fire Detection with Alarm System features a 25-meter sampling pipe with multiple sampling points. This system uses a suction fan to draw air from the protected area into the pipe network via holes in the pipes. The sampling points are distributed throughout the coach, covering the driver cab, passenger area, lavatories, doorways, and electrical cabinets. Each coach's pantry section includes a Heat Activated Sampling Point (HASP). Additionally, Photoelectric Smoke Detectors (point-type smoke detectors) are installed in the electrical cabinets. 4.1.1.2.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-1 (Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat Coaches)
text: The "Maintenance Fault“ of analog smoke sensors, is generated when there is a fault relating to the analog value of the device. This usually happens when the device fails calibration. For calibration to fail it generally means that the device has become too contaminated to be compensated for and requires maintenance. The OEM recommends removing the device from its base and connecting it to the handheld programmer (TCH-B200), to determine the analog value. The analog value will be displayed and, if relatively clean, should be in the low 60's. If it is significantly higher, then it will require cleaning.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-1 (Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat Coaches)
text: After cleaning and reassembling the device, once again connect it to the handheld programmer and read the analog value. If the value is now in the low 60's then it can be refitted and should operate fine. If not then it may indeed be faulty and need to be replaced. Removal of Outer Cover and Smoke Chamber for Maintenance If the wire mesh smoke chamber cover in a photoelectric smoke sensor gets heavily contaminated with large particles such as dust, soot, etc this could compromise the sensitivity of the device. The sensor is constructed as two halves, the device itself and its outer cover. 2 1 To access the smoke chamber, the outer cover needs to be separated from the device with the help of the Outer Cover Removal Tool. text: The HOCHIKI – FIRELINK 25 monitors the airflow of the aspirating system in the unit, ensuring that the system remains operational and sensitive to smoke detection.  A fault indication is triggered, and a Low Flow Error is recorded in the data log of the unit if the airflow value falls below the Low Flow Limit Parameters, which may suggest a blocked inlet pipe.  A fault indication is triggered, and a High Flow Error is recorded in the data log of the unit if the airflow value exceeds the High Flow Limit Parameters, potentially indicating a loose or damaged inlet pipe.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-1 (Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat Coaches)
text: Data log may be downloaded from the aspirating smoke detection unit for checking the airflow abnormalities of the aspirating system. Please refer to para – 4.1.2.6 for downloading the data log from HOCHIKI – FIRELINK 25 1. The airflow through the aspirating smoke detection unit shall be monitored to detect leakage or obstruction on the sampling device or sampling point(s). 1. Aspirating smoke detection unit - The aspirating smoke detection unit under test is set up in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. 2. Anemometer - To measure the normal airflow value (Fn) by a calibrated flow meter such as an anemometer with the worst-case sampling device. The minimum distance between the anemometer and the first sampling point is 30 cm. No sampling point shall be made between the aspirating smoke detection unit and the anemometer. Page 38 of 87

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-1 (Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat Coaches)
text: 1. The normal airflow (Fn)(Lt./min.) shall be determined from the sampling configuration used for the fire test with the help of application software or anemometer. 2. The aspirating smoke detection unit under test shall be tested at the test flow rate (Ft) (i.e. Ft = Fn ± 10%) for testing the airflow monitoring. 3. For an aspirating smoke detection unit under test that has a memorized normal flow, The Fn shall be entered into the memory in accordance with normal operating instructions for the detection system. This shall only be done once at the start of each test and shall not be done during/after the conditioning. 4. For decreased flow, the volumetric airflow is decreased from Fn by 20%, which shall be observed through application software or an anemometer installed between the sampling pipe and aspirating smoke detection unit. 5. For increased flow, the volumetric airflow is increased from Fn by 20%, which shall be observed through application software or an anemometer installed between the sampling pipe and detection system unit.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-1 (Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat Coaches)
text: 1. When the volumetric air flow reading in the system reaches the value of Fn - 20%, the aspirating smoke detection unit shall generate an airflow fault signal. 2. When the volumetric air flow reading in the system reaches the value of Fn + 20%, the aspirating smoke detection unit shall generate an airflow fault signal.

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-1 (Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat Coaches)
text: The Aerosol Fire Detection and Suppression System, on activation rapidly releases aerosol to extinguish the fire, thereby preventing damage to the coach and equipment. Aerosol Fire Detection and Suppression Systems have several key constructional features that enable their effective operation. These features are:  Aerosol Generator: The core component where the aerosol is produced. It typically contains a solid aerosol-forming compound.  Thermal Activation Device: This device activates the aerosol generator upon reaching a specific temperature, initiating the production of the aerosol. It enables the system to respond quickly to fire conditions.  Mounting Hardware: Brackets and supports that secure the aerosol generator and other components in place, ensuring stability and proper positioning for optimal performance. 1 3 2

title: Maintenance Manual for FSDS and FDSS Volume-1 (Vande Bharat & Amrit Bharat Coaches)
section: Aerosol Generator with Thermal Activation Device
text: The aerosol is produced in a generator that is activated by a thermal device when the required temperature is reached. It suppresses the fire through a combination of chemical and physical mechanisms without harming the environment. The aerosol is an ultra-fine component that remains suspended in the area, offering protection against re-ignition and facilitating easy cleanup. These units are compact and eliminate the need for costly pressure vessels, nozzles, and distribution piping typically required by other fire suppression systems. Page 45 of 87

text: 5.1.1.1. I. Bulb Thermal Actuator (BTA) The BTA combines both detection and activation for a single condensed aerosol generator. When a fire occurs, the temperature inside the enclosure reaches a pre- selected detection temperature, at this temperature the BTA’s bulb bursts, mechanically activating the generator. 1 4 2 5 3 II. Thermo Cable / Cord The thermo cable, also known as the thermo cord typically consists of a heat- sensitive material. This material is engineered to trigger the aerosol generator upon reaching the designated temperature, causing it to release the fire-suppressing aerosol. 1 2 Page 46 of 87 III. Manual/Thermal Activation Head This activation device is designed to activate the aerosol generator either manually or thermally, providing flexibility in fire suppression operations. Its activation modes are mentioned below: a. Manual Activation: This allows the user to manually initiate the aerosol release by pulling out the pull-pin. b. Thermal Activation: Automatically activates when it detects a specific temperature, ensuring the system responds quickly to fire conditions. 1 2

text: 5.1.1.5. ● After discharge, allow a minimum agent holding time of 10 minutes before ventilating the hazard space. ● Always have backup portable fire extinguishers on hand for use in the unlikely event of fire re-ignition. ● Ventilate the hazard area thoroughly by forced ventilation or by opening doors and windows. ● Inspect that all fires have been extinguished and that there are no localized hot spots or other sources of re-ignition present. ● Any minor amounts of agent residue not removed during ventilation should be thoroughly vacuumed, blown, brushed, or washed away (as appropriate). ● Exhausted aerosol generators will remain quite hot to the touch after discharge. They can be removed by wearing suitable hand protection. Caution: ● Do not touch aerosol generators within 15 minutes after the end of the discharge. The generator metal surfaces may be hot enough to cause injury to unprotected skin. ● Ensure the fire is completely extinguished before ventilating the hazard space. ● Ventilate thoroughly or use a self-contained breathing apparatus before entering.

Sub: Standardization of 2 Amp circuit breaker in FSDS system for IR AC coaches. Ref: (i) Railway Board's letter no. 76/M(C)/137/31 Vol. V dated 10.09.2024. (ii) This office letter of even no. dated: 23.09.24. (iii) This office letter of even no. dated: 12.08.24. On subject of provision of MCB in FSDS system, Railway Board vide reference (i) advised RDSO to examine the capacity issue of MCB in 110V FSDS/FDSS circuit of LHB coaches. In this regard, RDSO recommendations were submitted to the Railway Board via letter reference as (ii). Further, during the review meeting held on 25.09.24 and 26.09.24 at the Railway Board, the issue regarding the capacity of MCB in the 110V FSDS/FDSS circuit of LHB coaches was discussed.

title: RDSO Circular: Standardization of 2A MCB in FSDS System
section: RDSO Circular: Standardization of 2A MCB in FSDS System
text: Based on the deliberations, Railway Board advised RDSO to re-iterate the instructions contained in letter at ref (ii) to Zonal Railways for compliance. Accordingly, the following actions are to be followed for Standardization of 2 Amp circuit breaker in FSDS system with immediate effect: (i) In coaches, where no MCB was fitted by the supplier during initial installation of the FSDS system in the coaches, 2 Amp MCB with limiter module has to be provided by the supplier free of cost. (ii) In coaches, wherein circuit breaker other than of 2 Amp rating has been fitted during initial installation of the FSDS system, 2 Amp MCB with limiter module to be procured by Zonal Railways through OEMs to replace the originally fitted MCB. A budgetary rate reference from one of the suppliers is attached for your reference Additionally, it is also requested that this work should be carried out in conjunction with the other works including segregation work for positive and negative wires associated with the FSDS system, as also advised in the RDSO letter referenced (iii). Following google sheet is prepared to monitor this work.

Ref: PS & EMU Directorate letter no. EL/6.8.21 dated 15.07.2024 (copy enclosed). 1. Various cases have been reported by Zonal Railways wherein provision of MCB from power supply point to FSDS and separate conduits of positive and negative wire have not been done during installation of FSDS system. In this regard, relevant clauses of RDSO specification are reproduced below: Clause 8 (Section-A) of RDSO specification no. RDSO/2008/CG-04 deals with Supplier/OEM's responsibility.

title: RDSO Circular: Standardization of 2A MCB in FSDS System
section: RDSO Circular: Standardization of 2A MCB in FSDS System
text: Clause 8 (Section-A) of RDSO specification no. RDSO/2008/CG-04 deals with Supplier/OEM's responsibility. As per Clause 8.4 Supplier/OEM is responsible "For ensuring that the equipments/systems do not lead to unsafe or hazardous conditions for IR passengers & equipments". Further, as per clause 8.1 (Section-A) "The Supplier/OEM shall be completely responsible for the execution of the contract strictly in accordance with the terms of this specification and the conditions of contract, notwithstanding any approval which purchaser or the Inspecting Officer may have given". Above makes it amply clear that Supplier/OEM must ensure availability of all safety precaution while installing the FSDS system. 2. Additionally, as per Clause 1.7 (Section-B) of spec no. RDSO/2008/CG-04(Rev-5) following needs to be ensured: a) The control supply to the Fire Detection System will be provided from Terminal Block (TB) X1 of Switch Board Cabinet (SBC) for LHB AC coaches and TB-4 for ICF AC coaches through DC MCB of adequate rating. The MCB shall be always in 'on' position. b) Positive and negative wire of 110 V DC supply shall be segregated by placing them in separate conduits. 3.

title: RDSO Circular: Standardization of 2A MCB in FSDS System
section: RDSO Circular: Standardization of 2A MCB in FSDS System
text: The MCB shall be always in 'on' position. b) Positive and negative wire of 110 V DC supply shall be segregated by placing them in separate conduits. 3. PS & EMU Directorate of RDSO have also issued clarification for provision of power supply and MCB for FSDS system (copy enclosed).

title: RDSO Circular: Standardization of 2A MCB in FSDS System
section: RDSO Circular: Standardization of 2A MCB in FSDS System
text: In view of the above, it is advised that MCB for power supply connection and provision of separate conduits must be implemented to ensure reliability of FSDS system. Accordingly, Zonal Railways are advised to instruct the Suppliers/OEMs of FSDS system to ensure the compliance of above. This is for your information and further necessary action please. Vide reference above, ECR at its letter under reference, has pointed out issues for Operationalization of FSDS during dead attach movement of coaches. The matter has been examined and the precautions required to be followed are given as under: A. If the coaches are detached for sick-line attention, SS-I/SS-II/SS-III schedule or any dead attach movement for parent depot, following activities to be followed:

title: Operationalisation of FSDS during Dead Attach Movement of Coaches
section: Operationalisation of FSDS during Dead Attach Movement of Coaches
text: (i) Coach to be moved as empty in a locked condition. (ii) MCB of FSDS is to be switched “OFF”. (iii) The connection of FSDS with its battery (Wago terminal no. 1) should be disconnected. (iv) Brake valve of FSDS is to be isolated. (v) A sticker is also to be pasted on FSDS panel. The sticker shall be as under: “MCB of FSDS is switched “OFF” and Wago (Terminal no. 1) connection is disconnected. Brake valve is also isolated”. B. Whenever coaches are fit to be attached again with rake, following needs to be ensured during attachment in rake: a) Brake valve to be in normal functioning position (Handle position to open). b) Cable to be connected to Wago terminal no. 1 and MCB of FSDS is to be Switched “ON”. c) Sticker pasted on FSDS panel etc. to be removed. The pictorial view along with work instruction of the above is enclosed herewith Annexure-1. The above guidelines, if required will be reviewed based upon Zonal Railways feedback. title: Handbook on Wheel Slide Protection Device (WSP)
text: WSP system is the vital part of LHB & other FIAT fitted bogie coaches. WSP system is recently introduced in Indian Railways. Proper up keeping and maintenance of WSP system is necessary to ensure reliability and availability of coaches. This Handbook on WSP system has been prepared by CAMTECH with the objective that those involved in maintenance of LHB & other FIAT bogie fitted coaches, must be aware of WSP system and its function with correct maintenance. This Hand Book not only describes in WSP system but care has been taken to explain basic thing about WSP system including introduction, working principle, testing procedure etc. Technological up gradation and learning is a continuous process. Hence feel free to write to us for any addition/modifications or in case you have any suggestion to improve the Hand Book, your contribution in this direction shall be highly appreciated. title: Handbook on Wheel Slide Protection Device (WSP)
text: LHB coaches have been introduced in services on some of the premier trains on Indian Railways with state of art features. One of the important feature provided in these coaches are Initially, coaches turned out by production units were having two types of WSP’s namely supplied by (a) M/s Knorr Bremse India limited & (b) M/s SAB WABCO India ltd. During initial supplies Parrizi type processor was received with M/s Knorr Bremse air brake system whereas Sab Wabco with its own. During further developments, railways started using processors manufactured by M/s Knorr Bremse with its own air brake system & in the mean time, M/s Faiveley has taken over M/s Sab Wabco. Therefore, presently railways is having three types of processors (WSP’s) in service: 1. M/s Knorr Bremse India Ltd. 2. M/s Knorr Parrizi India Ltd. 3. M/s Faiveley India Ltd. (earlier known as M/s Sab Wabco) 2 After introduction in services, it is noticed that, performance of WSP specifically Knorr Parrizi system was not up to the mark & even firm was not able to give service support due to poor response from the OEM. In view of above, Parrizi type WSP are being replaced with Knorr Bremse system.

title: Handbook on Wheel Slide Protection Device (WSP)
text: In view of above, Parrizi type WSP are being replaced with Knorr Bremse system. Presently, railways is having mainly two types of WSP System. WSP control unit is a combination of various electronic cards. This unit is housed in electrical control panel units. This unit is connected by means of various cables through various equipments

title: Handbook on Wheel Slide Protection Device (WSP)
text: During the course of brake application, there are possibilities of skidding/sliding/locking of individual axle. In these cases adhesion between the rails & wheels plays vital roll. Above situations are likely to cause damage to wheel sets with increased braking distance. The main purpose of using the WSPs is to utilize the available adhesion. The WSPs provided in the system avoids wheel sliding, also cuts the maintenance cost. Speed sensors, the part of the system detect the speed of the wheel & sends signal to the processor unit. The processor unit evaluates the received signal from speed sensor of the vehicle & generates signals enabling the dump valve/antiskid valves to control the brake cylinder pressure in case of any locking/skidding. The control on the brake cylinder pressure is instantaneous to the wheel to rail adhesion, keeping the wheels within their optimum range of skidding. The WSP has some of the major parts.

The gap can be adjusted with the help of shims & measured through the peephole in axle box cover. The other end of the speed sensor i.e. cable is connected to junction box in car. title: Handbook on Wheel Slide Protection Device (WSP)
text: A phonic wheel is installed on one end of each axle. The phonic wheel is a toothed wheel (gear type). The purpose of this toothed wheel is to alter the internal inductance of the adjacent sensor. The change in internal inductance is evaluated as axle speed of various axles on a coach. During fitment, concentric movement of phonic wheel should be ensured. The eccentric movement of phonic wheel may cause signal errors, damage of speed sensor probe.

title: Handbook on Wheel Slide Protection Device (WSP)
text: Microprocessor is the heart of the WSP system. This gathers the signals from phonic wheel & speed sensors, evaluates the vehicle speed. Moreover, during brake application, it monitors & bridges the sharp drop of speed of a particular axle/wheel, enabling the dump valve to control/adjust the brake cylinder pressure. 5 Each processor is provided with LED display & some test buttons. This LED displays various codes which can be decoded & the health of WSP system can be evaluated.

title: Handbook on Wheel Slide Protection Device (WSP)
text: A dump valve is provided for each axle of the vehicle. These dump valves are a type of solenoid valves, connected with the air pressure line of brake cylinder. Dump valve/antiskid valve should be fitted close to the brake cylinders. These dump valves allow to deplete the air available in brake cylinder line during brake application based on the signals from WSP microprocessor.

title: Handbook on Wheel Slide Protection Device (WSP)
text: By pressing the keys on MMI, three different test runs can be performed. The test runs are terminated automatically when a speed signal higher than 03 kmph is identified. By pressing the key “S2” on MMI for about one sec, the valve control test run starts. The display will show “8888” for the first three seconds & then switches to “89”. Faults found by the test are displayed at the end of the run. Volatile faults that have occurred at some time on the move and disappeared again in the meantime (e.g. loose contacts), are displayed as number “95”. After the test run has been completed, the code “99” is again shown on the display. All the brake cylinders of axles 1 - 4 are vented in succession. The alignment of anti skid valve and speed 30 sensor of all the axles starting from axle 1 are checked. Any failure will result in inaccurate axle speeds being measured which causes false pressure values are set in the anti skid valves.

title: Handbook on Wheel Slide Protection Device (WSP)
text: 1.7.2(A)   Retrieving faults from memory The display return code “99” if the fault memory is empty & no keys are pressed. The display shows code number “95”, if any volatile faults are in memory. Press key “S1” to start the query. To begin with, the display reads “8888”. All current faults are displayed for three seconds each. The display subsequently reads “95” & then shows the volatile faults. 1.7.2(B)   Erasing faults from memory The fault memory is erased when the erase key “S3” is pressed for about one second. However, persistent faults will be entered instantly again in the fault memory.

source: FT0027800-003 E00 MUM Rev A01, 26/02/2019, Faiveley/Wabtec
text: 4.1 Train operators are fully aware of the problems resulting from insufficient wheel/rail adhesion when a train is accelerating or braking. During a constant braking force application, dependent upon the coefficient of friction available at the wheel/rail interface, the wheel sets could start to slide. Sliding causes damage to the wheel sets (flats) and increases the stopping distance. Technological advances in the area of microelectronics and the use of microcomputers enable the WSP function of a braking system to be enhanced by maximizing the use of the available adhesion. In addition, benefits can be gained by widening the function and by improving the diagnostics. The latter assists in cutting the costs of the maintenance work. Based on long experience of rolling stock micro electronic systems, the rack version of AEF G2 WSP control unit was developed. This system is able to make optimum use of available adhesion when braking, thereby optimizing the stopping distances and preventing locked (sliding) wheels and the resulting damage.

text: Axle speed of rotation is measured and evaluated separately within a speed range of 2 to 400 km/h. Axle speeds are compared with a reference speed which is a calculated value based on the real axle speeds. The comparison between these speed signals determines whether or not an axle is about to enter in to a slide mode. The axles speeds are measured via speed sensors and phonic wheels, all located at the axle ends. Solenoid valves (dump valves) are connected to the brake pipe close to the brake cylinders but mounted on the underside of the car body. These valves control the increase and decrease of the air pressure in the brake cylinders to assure the optimum pressure in the brake cylinders and maximized braking for the prevailing wheel/rail interface conditions, and thus prevent sliding from occurring. The dump valves are controlled by a 24 V nominal voltage from an internal power supply. The dump valve drive circuits are bipolar i.e. each positive and each negative wire has its own amplifier; all amplifiers are monitored by hardware watchdog circuits to fulfill the safety requirements demanded by railway operators.

source: FT0027800-003 E00 MUM Rev A01, 26/02/2019, Faiveley/Wabtec
text: Watchdog circuits supervise the correct switching of the amplifiers, if a malfunction occurs it disconnects them. The control engineering, measurement data acquisition, internal system supervision an all additional features are carried out by a micro controller, updating the measurement data every 20ms. This ensures correct function for speeds between 2 and 400 km/h. Digital signal outputs allow enhanced data evaluation for non WSP activities, a speed dependent door automatic function and toilet control are some of the applications to be mentioned in this project. 4.2

source: FT0027800-003 E00 MUM Rev A01, 26/02/2019, Faiveley/Wabtec
text: The function of WBI board is to control and manage the WSP functionalities. It is composed by two sections: ▪ Speed input section: The board has 4 speed input channels to measure the individual axle speeds. The board provides isolated 15 V to supply the sensors. Each speed channel is equipped with control circuits to check if the sensor is connected, disconnected or damaged. ▪ Dump valve drive section: The board has 4 digital output channels to drive the dump valves with open/short circuit protection. Each WBI board can control two dump valves; each control channel is organized in two outputs: fill and vent. The fill stage is controlled by a hardware watchdog that determines the maximum valve excitation time (9.7 ± 0.2 s). Therefore, each channel is monitored by: o An interlock circuit to avoid that the vent valve is energized alone (forbidden condition); o A Life signal that enables the power supply of the channels only if the software is working properly (safety condition).

Part two of this manual describes the installation of the AEF G2 wheel slide protection system for Railway vehicles. Reference is made in this description to the AEF G2 WSP equipment and to all external components. It describes all of the mechanical work, and the electrical and pneumatic connections that need to be made ensure correct installation and function of the equipment.

text: Care must be taken to ensure that all components are correctly installed. Correct operation of the AEF G2 WSP system is dependent upon correct installation. Figure1 shows a schematic overview of the vehicle installation of the equipment and the system wiring diagram. The solenoids are marked with the designations 1-4 and the speed sensors and phonic wheels are indicated by G1 - G4.

title: AEF G2 WSP Maintenance/Use Manual - LHB Coaches Indian Railways
source: FT0027800-003 E00 MUM Rev A01, 26/02/2019, Faiveley/Wabtec
text: The AEF G2 WSP electronic module must be fitted in a horizontal position. Care must be taken to ensure that the electronic module is installed in a tamper proof dry cabinet or compartment in the vehicle. In choosing the installation position for the electronic module it is essential to ensure that the equipment cannot be splashed with any water at any time, including during vehicle cleaning process. Water penetration to the electronics may impair the performance of the system. The equipment is manufactured in accordance with protection class IP20. Installation of the electronic module is achieved by means of 4: M6 screws which pass through the slotted holes on either side of the electronic module casing, to fasten it firmly to the mounting surface of the vehicle. The equipment must be protected from dampness and dust, and sufficient air circulation must be maintained for cooling purposes. The housing must be suitably electrically earthed with a minimum cable cross section of 6 mm².

title: AEF G2 WSP Maintenance/Use Manual - LHB Coaches Indian Railways
source: FT0027800-003 E00 MUM Rev A01, 26/02/2019, Faiveley/Wabtec
text: The pressure switch has to be installed at a protected area in the wagon. An installation of the pressure switch beneath the wagon is not allowed due to the protection group of IP 54. A dump valve is to be provided for each axle of the vehicle. The valve is fastened by screws to the vehicle body. It should not be mounted to the bogie. Two M10 x 1.5 x 6H tapped holes in the valve are provided for mounting the valve housing. Figure 2 shows one way of positioning a dump valve.

text: Ensure that the valve is mounted with the vent outlet (E) facing downwards. Before connecting piping to C and D on the support bracket a blast of air should be blown through the piping system to ensure it is dirt-free and clean. The piping connection "C" located on the valve support bracket should be connected to brake cylinder and "D" to the control valve (see fig. 3). The length of the brake hose between the brake cylinder and dump valve should not exceed 1.5 m.

title: AEF G2 WSP Maintenance/Use Manual - LHB Coaches Indian Railways

text: In the dump valve bracket, there are two chokes to regulate the apply and release time of brake. At the first commissioning of a new vehicle or when the brake cylinder area is modified, these timings should be measured. The measure can be made with a pressure transducer and an oscilloscope or with special equipment. The pressure transducer can be installed using a special arrangement. To release the brake cylinder pressure connect 24V to both coils. To fill the brake cylinder connect no voltage to any valve coil. Refer the dump valve cable drawing for further information. The release and apply times shall be measured under full brake cylinder pressure. The exhausting time should be min. 600, max. 800ms (from 100% to 10% pressure). The filling time should be min. 1000ms, max. 1200ms (from 0% to 90% pressure). The chokes must be changed when times out of this tolerance range are measured. When the time is to long there must be set in a bigger diameter. When the time is to short there must be set in a smaller diameter. Normally the diameter of the exhausting side (brake cylinder) is bigger than the diameter of the filling side (supply pipe).

title: AEF G2 WSP Maintenance/Use Manual - LHB Coaches Indian Railways

text: Normally the diameter of the exhausting side (brake cylinder) is bigger than the diameter of the filling side (supply pipe). FT recommends installing the dump valves close to the brake cylinder because the piping length between valve and brake cylinder has great influences to the exhaust timings.

title: AEF G2 WSP Maintenance/Use Manual - LHB Coaches Indian Railways

text: Ensure that the "O" ring seal is in place on the sensor head. Insert speed sensor into the hole provided in the axle end cover of each axle and bolt it into position. Check that the distance between the sensor head and the phonic wheel is within the range 1.0 ± 0.5 mm when the sensor head is bolted tightly. If adjustment is required shims should be placed between the sensor head and the axle end cover until the gap is correct when the sensor head bolted tightly. Care must be taken to ensure that the gap distance between phonic wheel and speed sensor is set correctly too small a distance can cause mechanical damage to the sensor, whereas too large a gap will impair the functioning. The electric cable from the speed sensor is attached with a PG screw (PG 13.5) to the terminal box fitted below the vehicle body. Wiring has to be carried out as per the Electrical scheme FZ0205900- E00.

title: AEF G2 WSP Maintenance/Use Manual - LHB Coaches Indian Railways
source: FT0027800-003 E00 MUM Rev A01, 26/02/2019, Faiveley/Wabtec
text: The phonic wheel is to be fitted on the axle end by bolts to the normal Railway standard. The Phonic wheel should be fitted to the axle where the speed sensor is fitted. The strip terminal is to be wired as per the wiring diagram FZ0205900-E00. The isolation layers are to be removed from the individual leads, and the non insulated lead ends secured in the binders. Ensure that the screws of the individual binders are firmly tightened, and the cables are protected from tension loading. In addition, ensure that the shielding of the cable is cut back to a minimum length (as short as possible), i.e. remove cover and shielding only just up to the strip terminal.

title: AEF G2 WSP Maintenance/Use Manual - LHB Coaches Indian Railways
source: FT0027800-003 E00 MUM Rev A01, 26/02/2019, Faiveley/Wabtec
text: After verification of correctness of the installation work and piping and the wiring carried out, turn on the AEF G2 wheel slide protection system and it will carry out a self-test. The following tests are available: 3.1 Start condition: At power-up OR automatic start 3 min after the train stop on condition that the reference speed has previously exceeded 50 km/h. End condition: if test is completed or if train speed becomes higher than 3 km/h. Sequence of test: During the test of each dump valve the discharge has a 20 ms duration to avoid a reduction of brake effort. All the faults present during the test will be displayed at the end of the automatic test.

section: Figure 2 : Front view of WSP System
text: The WSP control unit is used to provide anti-slide control for complete train or single coaches. The WSP control unit is composed by a 19”rack unit with a mother board mounted on the back side and a set of plug-in cards that can be inserted and extracted without dismounting the rack. The rack is fitted with fixation points that allow installing it into the supporting structure. The front panel of the display plug-in unit of the WSP control unit contains a four-digit alphanumeric display for the local indication of errors. The errors buffer can be browsed using the four pushbuttons.

source: FT0027800-003 E00 MUM Rev A01, 26/02/2019, Faiveley/Wabtec
text: The electronic unit does not require any maintenance: All internal and external components are continuously checked by the self test routine, so that no manual inspection is necessary. The battery should be replaced to keep the functionality of storing process data in the internal RAM. Further functions of the WSP-System are not affected by an empty/drained battery. In general it should be renounced an unnecessary disassembly of the Wheel slide protection device, because separating and restoration of the electrical connections are causing the risk of arising failures. During the regular car inspection a visual check of the electronic unit should be carried through. In this case one has to take care that the display shows code “9999" to ensure there are no errors. If for some reason a different code is displayed then reference should be made to the trouble shooting section of the manual and follow the instructions given there.

text: The Dump Valve is used to prevent the wheel blocking in situations of low adhesion between wheel and rail. It is used to regulate the pressure in the brake cylinders in order to maximize the braking effort for any given wheel/rail interface coefficient of friction, thus achieving the shortest stopping distance and preventing wheel flats. The dump valve can be fitted with bracket. The Dump valve and the connecting pipe between the distributor and the brake cylinder must be checked regularly for damages and leakage. The function of the Dump valves can be tested by launching the test by push button on the CPU board when the train is in standstill condition or launching the test by means of monitoring software.

text: The speed sensor can be installed in any angle maintaining the radial position between the sensor probe and the phonic wheel. It counts the number of rotation of the phonic wheel and sends the corresponding speed value. The single speed sensor has one sensing transducer or probe and the double speed sensor has two such transducers.

During the regular inspection of the car a visual check of the speed sensor should be carried through. Following steps to be followed: 1. Visual check of the sensor’s damages, in particular: ▪ sensor head ▪ damage of protection hose ▪ bending of the protection hose 2. Checking of the correct assembling of the sensor’s (distance to the phonic wheel) 3. Function check of speed sensor while WSP Electronic is switched on (modulation) and with the manual test as per “Part 2: Installation and Start–Up”.

text: WSP system for LHB coaches Speed sensors The speed sensor scans a ferromagnetic rotating gear (tooth module / Phonic wheel) that is centered over the axle. It works without physical contact and does not wear. The frequency of the digital current signal is directly proportional to the circumferential speed of the rotating gear. When the vehicle is at standstill, the output current from the sensor assumes the value ( low & High ). The control unit monitors the speed sensors for correct operation at both standstill and on the move. Open circuits and faults to ground are identified. The electronic part of the speed sensors withstands short-circuiting, prevents reversal of its polarity and resists EMC interference. Rotating gears with 80 teeth are used as standard. **Check Dump Valve connections.**

**Check the connections of the speed sensor, if found short/ open circuit, fix it.**

**If connections are okay, check gap between the phonic wheel and speed sensor, it should be between 0.9mm to 1.4mm. If**
**abnormal gap is detected, correct it.**

**If everything above is okay, JFP card can be faulty.**

**Check if the Dump Valve Exhaust coil is shorted. If it is, replace the Dump Valve.**

**If the coil is fine, look for any shorted wire and fix it.**


**Check if the Dump Valve Exhaust coil is open. If it is, replace the Dump Valve.**

**If the coil is fine, look for any open wire and fix it.**

**If the coil and wiring are okay, re-check the system if problem persists, replace the respective JOP Card.**| |**2.3**|**For Axle 2**|**For Axle 2**| |**3.3**|**For Axle 3**|**For Axle 3**| |**4.3**|**For Axle 4**|**For Axle 4**|

A fire incidence has taken place recently in Pantry Car No. 213650 of train no. 22805/06 ANVT BBS Exp while the train was stabled in yard of ANVT station. During subsequent examination it was found that solenoid valve of FDSS system was disconnected due to which the automatic fire suppression system could not get activated. Disconnection of solenoid valve is required only during testing of system during SS-1 schedule.

title: Functionality of Automatic FDSS fitted in Pantry & Power Cars
section: Functionality of Automatic FDSS fitted in Pantry & Power Cars
text: Disconnection of solenoid valve is required only during testing of system during SS-1 schedule. Other than it, any such disconnection is not permitted. In this regard, RDSO is amending the relevant specification for including provision of audio alert in case of disconnection of solenoid valve. However, as an interim measure, sealing of solenoid valve and its intactness to be checked during primary maintenance. The sealing shall be acknowledged especially by Pantry Manager in pantry cars before departure of train from originating stations. The photographs for sealing are given below for ready reference. Though the work of providing sealing arrangement in Pantry & Power car should be completed on urgent basis, however pantry cars should be completed on priority. Further, RCF/KXH has already issued a CAI for Retro fitment of locking arrangement for isolating cock of Aspiration type smoke/Fire detection with Alarm system in LHB AC Coaches vide letter no. MD 46111 dated 22.05.2024 (copy enclosed). This work is also to be completed at earliest. DA: As above (Anurag Malik) Jt. Director/SS/Carriage 06.06.24 Copy to: JDME/Chg.

Sub: Guidelines for upgradation of Automatic fire detection cum suppression system (FDSS) as specified in Amendment-1 as per IS/RDSO/CG/S/22001 for existing Pantry car & Generator cum brake van of IR coaches (ICF and LHB design). Ref: This office letter no. MC/ACF/Fire Supprn/PC dated 09.09.2024. 1. Based upon the feedback of Zonal Railways and detailed discussions with stakeholders, RDSO has amended the specification no. IS/RDSO/CG/S/22001 duly addressing the issues pointed out by ZRs. Following main features have been incorporated in Amendment-1 of RDSO specification no. IS/RDSO/CG/S/22001 issued on 09.09.24. a) Provision of Common interface/screen for status monitoring & standard format/error codes for data downloading through USB.

title: RDSO Guidelines for FDSS Upgradation — Amendment-1 of IS/RDSO/CG/S/22001 (Pantry Cars & Generator-cum-Brake Vans, ICF & LHB)
section: RDSO Guidelines for FDSS Upgradation — Amendment-1 of IS/RDSO/CG/S/22001 (Pantry Cars & Generator-cum-Brake Vans, ICF &
text: a) Provision of Common interface/screen for status monitoring & standard format/error codes for data downloading through USB. b) Audio indication along with capturing of isolation/disconnection of Nitrogen cylinder in data log. c) The extension of automatic fire suppression system in the luggage area of power car and manual suppression system in the escorting staff area of power car/ storage area of pantry cars of IR coaches. 2. PUs have already been advised that all future procurement of FDSS system for IR Pantry car & Generator cum brake van of IR coaches will be with the amended specification however the upgradations incorporated in the amended specification are retrofittable & the features incorporated are for ease in system monitoring and maintenance as well as to improve reliability and thus, are recommended for being implemented in existing IR coaches also. 3. Railway Board is requested to nominate any of the PU as nodal to carry out awarding of the work related with upgradation of FDSS systems through OEM/Suppliers in existing IR Pantry car & Generator cum brake van of IR coaches.

IS/RDSO/CG/S/22001 in existing Pantry car & Generator cum brake van of IR coaches (ICF and LHB design): A. Design requirement 1. USB 2.0 port The size of common interface panel should be within 150mmX100mm for indications & data download panel. Indicators should be 22mm Panel mounted LED indicators (pilot light) and USB port should be covered with protective cover to avoid ingress of dust. b) The luggage compartment of power car will be protected with Linear Heat Detector (LHD) cable. Activation of suppression system would take place automatically in luggage area whenever fire signal is received from luggage compartment. Provision of High pressure water mist based fire suppression system along with associated piping, solenoid valves, sectioning valves, nozzles etc. in luggage area of power car is included in scope of supply. c) Provision of High pressure water mist based fire suppression system along with associated piping, solenoid valves, sectioning valves, nozzles is also to be provided in escorting staff area/storage area of Pantry car.

Various cases have been reported by Zonal Railways wherein provision of MCB from power supply point to FSDS and separate conduits of positive and negative wire have not been done during installation of FSDS system. In this regard, relevant clauses of RDSO specification are reproduced below: Clause 8 (Section-A) of RDSO specification no. RDSO/2008/CG-04 deals with Supplier/OEM's responsibility.

title: RDSO to PCMEs: Power Supply MCB for FSDS Fire Detection
section: RDSO to PCMEs: Power Supply MCB for FSDS Fire Detection
text: Clause 8 (Section-A) of RDSO specification no. RDSO/2008/CG-04 deals with Supplier/OEM's responsibility. As per Clause 8.4 Supplier/OEM is responsible "For ensuring that the equipments/systems do not lead to unsafe or hazardous conditions for IR passengers & equipments". Further, as per clause 8.1 (Section-A) "The Supplier/OEM shall be completely responsible for the execution of the contract strictly in accordance with the terms of this specification and the conditions of contract, notwithstanding any approval which purchaser or the Inspecting Officer may have given". Above makes it amply clear that Supplier/OEM must ensure availability of all safety precaution while installing the FSDS system. 2. Additionally, as per Clause 1.7 (Section-B) of spec no. RDSO/2008/CG-04(Rev-5) following needs to be ensured: a) The control supply to the Fire Detection System will be provided from Terminal Block (TB) X1 of Switch Board Cabinet (SBC) for LHB AC coaches and TB-4 for ICF AC coaches through DC MCB of adequate rating. The MCB shall be always in 'on' position. b) Positive and negative wire of 110 V DC supply shall be segregated by placing them in separate conduits. 3.

title: RDSO to PCMEs: Power Supply MCB for FSDS Fire Detection
section: RDSO to PCMEs: Power Supply MCB for FSDS Fire Detection
text: The MCB shall be always in 'on' position. b) Positive and negative wire of 110 V DC supply shall be segregated by placing them in separate conduits. 3. PS & EMU Directorate of RDSO have also issued clarification for provision of power supply and MCB for FSDS system (copy enclosed).

title: RDSO to PCMEs: Power Supply MCB for FSDS Fire Detection

RDSO/2008/CG-04/(Rev-06). Clause 11.4 of RDSO specification no. RDSO/2008/CG-04/(Rev-06) contains the proforma for testing of automatic smoke/ fire detection system during installation and commissioning on a designated coach. The proforma contains following tests which are to be carried out during commissioning i. Smoke detection test for each sampling point. ii. Checking of the threshold value. iii. Airflow monitoring test. iv. Testing of Brake application. v. Hot wire test.

title: Over-heated Wire Test for FSDS fitted in IR AC Coaches
section: Over-heated Wire Test for FSDS fitted in IR AC Coaches
text: ii. Checking of the threshold value. iii. Airflow monitoring test. iv. Testing of Brake application. v. Hot wire test. During a recent fire incidence, the FSDS system was found not properly installed which indicates that installation & commissioning was carried out without completing all the tests as mentioned in the proforma. Further, Hot wire test is an important test for testing of the FSDS system by simulating electrical fire and accordingly Zonal Railways must ensure that all the test as per clause no 11.4 of RDSO spec no. RDSO/2008/CG-04/(Rev-06) including Hot wire test are carried out during installation & commissioning of FSDS system on designated coaches. In view of above, following corrective action should be taken with immediate effect for improving reliability of FSDS system: 1. Zonal Railways to ensure complete testing of the system as per proforma at the time of installation & commissioning of FSDS system on a coach. Drive is already

text: going on Fire safety including checking of working of FSDS system and accordingly, if electrical connections in any coach are not found proper, all tests as per above proforma to be carried out 2. 100 % Over heated wire test should be carried out during POH of coaches. 3. Following activities should be made part of primary maintenance & to be included in maintenance form. a. CAI has already been issued by RCF to prevent unauthorized isolation of brake valve. Same to be checked during maintenance and isolation cases must be reported. (copy of CAI attached) b. FSDS Data log must be downloaded in every monthly schedule. One-month data must be preserved. 4. Further, RDSO has issued guidelines on subject of handling of dead attach movement of coaches fitted with FSDS system. The copy of the same is also enclosed herewith for ready reference of Zonal Railways. DA: as above Anurag 13.06.24 (Anurag Malik) Jt. The matter has been examined and the precautions required to be followed are given as under: A. If the coaches are detached for sick-line attention, SS-I/SS-II/SS-III schedule or any dead attach movement for parent depot, following activities to be followed:

title: Over-heated Wire Test for FSDS fitted in IR AC Coaches
section: Over-heated Wire Test for FSDS fitted in IR AC Coaches
text: (i) Coach to be moved as empty in a locked condition. (ii) MCB of FSDS is to be switched “OFF”. (iii) The connection of FSDS with its battery (Wago terminal no. 1) should be disconnected. (iv) Brake valve of FSDS is to be isolated. (v) A sticker is also to be pasted on FSDS panel. The sticker shall be as under: “MCB of FSDS is switched “OFF” and Wago (Terminal no. 1) connection is disconnected. Brake valve is also isolated”. B. Whenever coaches are fit to be attached again with rake, following needs to be ensured during attachment in rake: a) Brake valve to be in normal functioning position (Handle position to open). b) Cable to be connected to Wago terminal no. 1 and MCB of FSDS is to be Switched “ON”. c) Sticker pasted on FSDS panel etc. to be removed. The pictorial view along with work instruction of the above is enclosed herewith Annexure-1. The above guidelines, if required will be reviewed based upon Zonal Railways feedback. DA: As above (Anurag Malik) Jt. Director/SS /Carriage 06.06.24

RDSO/2008/CG-04: "The supplier/OEM shall be completely responsible for the execution of the contract strictly in accordance with the terms of this specification and the conditions of contract, not withstanding any approval which purchaser or the Inspecting Officer may have given". Additionally, as per Clause 8.4(Section-A) of RDSO specification no. RDSO/2008/CG-04: "For ensuring that the equipments/systems do not lead to unsafe or hazardous conditions for IR passengers & equipments". The specification clearly mandates that suppliers are bound to adhere to all requirements to ensure safety, reliability, and strict compliance of specification. Furthermore, as per Clause no. 1.7 (a) of Section-B of RDSO specification no. RDSO/2008/CG-04(Rev-5 onwards), it is categorically stated that, "The control supply to the Fire Detection System will be provided from Terminal Block (TB) X1 of the Switch Board Cabinet (SBC) for LHB AC coaches through DC MCB of adequate rating".

text: An unfortunate incidence of fire due to non-availability of MCB at supply take off point at SBC had occurred recently which is to be avoided in future. From the above, it is amply clear that MCB has to be provided at the point of power tapping from SBC panel for protection of 110V DC wiring for FSDS system and that Supplier is bound to carryout the work as per specification irrespective of an approval by purchaser. In this regard, vide letter under reference, instructions were issued for compliance of the above. Suppliers were also instructed regarding the same during meeting at Carriage Dte, RDSO on dated 18.10.24. However, it has been reported by Zonal Railways that suppliers are showing resistance for the compliance of the above. These observations highlight deviations from the specifications and guidelines issued by RDSO. Accordingly, it is hereby re-advised that compliance of already issued specifications and guidelines to be ensured without fail at the earliest. Any non-compliance is likely to result in punitive action. DA: As above (Anurag Malik) Jt. Director/SS/Carriage 27.11.24 Copy to:

title: RDSO: Compliance of Specification RDSO/2008/CG-04 & FSDS Guidelines (MCB / control supply from TB X1 of SBC)
section: RDSO: Compliance of Specification RDSO/2008/CG-04 & FSDS Guidelines (MCB / control supply from TB X1 of SBC)
text: Clause 8 (Section-A) of RDSO specification no. RDSO/2008/CG-04 deals with Supplier/OEM's responsibility. As per Clause 8.4 Supplier/OEM is responsible "For ensuring that the equipments/systems do not lead to unsafe or hazardous conditions for IR passengers & equipments". Further, as per clause 8.1 (Section-A) "The Supplier/OEM shall be completely responsible for the execution of the contract strictly in accordance with the terms of this specification and the conditions of contract, notwithstanding any approval which purchaser or the Inspecting Officer may have given". Above makes it amply clear that Supplier/OEM must ensure availability of all safety precaution while installing the FSDS system. 2. Additionally, as per Clause 1.7 (Section-B) of spec no. RDSO/2008/CG-04(Rev-5) following needs to be ensured: a) The control supply to the Fire Detection System will be provided from Terminal Block (TB) X1 of Switch Board Cabinet (SBC) for LHB AC coaches and TB-4 for ICF AC coaches through DC MCB of adequate rating. The MCB shall be always in 'on' position. b) Positive and negative wire of 110 V DC supply shall be segregated by placing them in separate conduits. 3.

title: RDSO: Air Gap Setting between Phonic Wheel and WSP Speed Sensor — standardised 0.9–1.4 mm for both makes
section: Air Gap setting between phonic wheel and WSP speed sensor
text: Railways have been facing difficulty in maintaining the gap between two different systems. The subject matter has been discussed with the OEMs to standardize the common gap between phonic wheel and speed sensor for their WSP system. M/s Faiveley Transport vide their letter No.FTRIL/Engg/RCF-WSP/2011-12 (copy enclosed) has confirmed that the gap in FTIL equipment also can be reduced to 0.9 to 1.4 mm with out any effect on the performance of the system. In view of the above, the air gap between phonic wheel and speed sensor for WSP system is standardized as 0.9 to 1.4mm for both the system.
