title: VB/SMI/E/06: VCB Isolation Procedure in Vande Bharat Trainset
section: VB/SMI/E/06: VCB Isolation Procedure in Vande Bharat Trainset
text: 1. It is a general practice to  reclose VCB by LP whenever “not all VCB closed” indication is noticed 2. Anyways, Repeated Reclosing of VCB by LP in case of tripping occurred by “Transformer primary over current fault” lead to repeated arcing at fault location and subsequent fire safety related issues . It is therefore  instructed to LP/ALP to restrain from reclosing the VCB in case of “ VCB tripping by – transformer primary over current fault” and follow the procedure B to isolate the BU in this particular case. 3. The procedure for checking the fault on which the VCB is tripped is explained in procedure A. Procedure A : Confirmation  of “Transformer primary over current fault”. a) Check if  “NOT ALL VCB CLOSED” Indication is ON in Indication Panel, 1 ANNEXURE 1. It is a general practice to reclose VCB by LP whenever “not all VCB closed” indication is noticed 2. Anyways, Repeated Reclosing of VCB by LP in case of tripping occurred by “Transformer primary over current fault” lead to repeated arcing at fault location and subsequent fire safety related issues .

title: VB/SMI/E/06: VCB Isolation Procedure in Vande Bharat Trainset
section: VB/SMI/E/06: VCB Isolation Procedure in Vande Bharat Trainset
text: It is therefore instructed to LP/ALP to restrain from reclosing the VCB in case of “ VCB tripping by – transformer primary over current fault” and follow the procedure B to isolate the BU in this particular case. 3. The procedure for checking the fault on which the VCB is tripped is explained in procedure A. Procedure A : Confirmation of “Transformer primary over current fault”. a) Check if “NOT ALL VCB CLOSED” Indication is ON in Indication Panel, Panel Components: - PANTO 1,4 UP (Yellow) - NOT ALL VCB CLOSED (Yellow) - EMR BRAKE (Red) - EMR OFF (Red) - MIN 1 PB APPLIED (Red) - MIN 1 AS FAILED (Blue) - MIN 1 BR APPLIED (Red) - MIN 1 DOOR OPENED (Red) - AC FAULT (Red) - PANTO 2,3 UP (Red) - MIN 1 VCB CLOSED (Blue) - RDM (Blue) - OHE AVAILABLE (Green) - ALL DOORS CLOSED (Green) - SINGLE UNIT OPERATION (Yellow) - TCN FAILURE (Red) 2 b)  Check for  fault message – " Transformer Primary over current fault” in the fault record row as shown below .

text: c) If  VCB has tripped with fault- “Transformer Primary over current fault” The VCB should not be reclosed and The particular BU to be isolated as per the procedure B. Note:  After isolation of Faulty BU the panto selector switch to be appropriately changed to ensure that remaining BUs are getting energized.  Isolation of BU to be re done after every BN recycle.  This shall be recorded in the Train register  and intimate to the depot for further course of action.  As an Exception, in case of  8 car VB rake or in case of unavoidable situations

title: VB/SMI/E/07: Winter Preparedness Drive for Vande Bharat Trainset
section: Winter preparedness drive for Vande Bharat Trains
text: VB/SMI/E/07 Dated :14.11.2024 INTEGRAL COACH FACTORY, CHENNAI - 600 038 No.MD/D/TrainSet/168/RBContract/186G Mobile no.9003141310 Mail id:dyceedicf@gmail.com Office of CDE/Elec. Dt :14.11.2024 PCEEs &PCMEs of all Zonal Railways Sub: Winter preparedness drive for Vande Bharat Trains These Instructions are being issued for undertaking essential precautions and special drive to check all Vande Bharat trains prior to the commencement of winter season, so that typical failures attributed to low temperature and fog do not occur and the desired level of reliability is maintained. 1. During all trip inspections or roof inspections whenever carried out, proper cleaning of roof-line & pantograph insulators (non-porcelain) with a lint-free wet & dry cloth for maintaining clean surface finish may be ensured by homing depot before onset of winter. 2. For Porcelain insulators, clean with lint-free cloth and apply Silicone oil to increase the hydrophobicity of insulator porcelain surface after cleaning. Use detergent for cleaning, if necessary to remove all adhered contamination and to provide the surface the nice original gloss. 3.

title: VB/SMI/E/07: Winter Preparedness Drive for Vande Bharat Trainset
section: Winter preparedness drive for Vande Bharat Trains
text: Use detergent for cleaning, if necessary to remove all adhered contamination and to provide the surface the nice original gloss. 3. Ensure joint checking of TC roof equipment (including pantographs, cleaning of roof insulators and roof bar etc.) and Roof HV cables with TRD staff at depots as a preventive measure. 4. Working of heaters to be ensured in Cab AC in both driving and non-driving cabs and all RMPUs along with their safety interlocks. 5. Proper level of oil in TFP and coolant in Traction Converter to be maintained. 6. Silica gel for Transformer must be in good condition. 7. All Air dryers must be in working order and isolation should not be permitted. 8. Draining of moisture from all MR and ensure free movement of drain cocks and proper functioning of Auto Drain valve. 9. Headlights are cleaned and proper focus along with intensity to be ensured. Ensure proper working of flasher light, marker light, etc. 10. Ensure the proper working of wipers. 11. Ensure Signal Exchange Lights are working. 12. Proper cleaning of look out glass and window glass before the Trainset leaves the Depot. 13. Re greasing of Stabilizer bar bearing in bogie shall be done. 14.

title: VB/SMI/E/12: Procedure for Dimming of Light in Vande Bharat Coaches
section: Operating procedure/Instructions for Dimming of light in Vande Bharat Train Set rakes
text: VB/SMI/E/12 Dated:08.02.2025 INTEGRAL COACH FACTORY, CHENNAI: 38 Mail : cdecicf@gmail.com Mobile: 9003141302 No. MD/D/Train Set/RB Contract/186G Office of the CDE/Elec., Dt. 08.02.2025 PCME/E.Rly Sub : Operating procedure/Instructions for Dimming of light in Vande Bharat Train Set rakes Ref: (i) Inspection of Train no. 22435 BSB-NDLS Vande Bharat express from CNB to NDLS on 03.02.2024 and issue of Inspection notes no 2024/EDME/Chg/Inspection notes/2 dt.06.02.2024 Based on inspection note in sl.12 of EDME/Chg vide letter under reference (i) ,Facility to dim the coach lights for better passenger comfort during early hours/late hours of the day in the VB train, is introduced in Rake-75 on trial basis which is running between Howrah and Baghalpur, which involves following modifications 1. Direct lighting (DL) & Indirect lighting (IDL) in compartment are segregated such that both DL circuits connected in BN lights circuit and both IDL circuits connected to BD lights circuit. 2. All IDL in compartment and all doorway lights &gangway lights will be ON when 50 % light is selected and all (DL+IDL) compartment will be ON when 100% light is selected in driver desk. 3.

title: VB/SMI/E/12: Procedure for Dimming of Light in Vande Bharat Coaches
section: Operating procedure/Instructions for Dimming of light in Vande Bharat Train Set rakes
text: 3. Dimming of light in passenger compartment (IDL only) can be done by selecting ‘50% light mode from driver desk 4. A local switch is provided in each coach to switch ON DL locally within the coach at the face of need during 50% light mode operated by driver. To ensure sufficient light for pantry staff to serve food during 50% light mode (dimming light mode), DL can be switched ON in any of the coaches by switching the local control switch for DL provided near ECC panel in each coach and behind CRW panel in DTC. The following operating Instructions are attached as Annexure A for dimming of lights in passenger compartment by Loco pilots/Train Crews. Zonal Railway can decide the operational requirement of DL & IDL as per the passenger feedback and issue necessary guidelines to train manager for dimming of lights in trainsets for the required period (early/late hours of the day) during the run. title: VB/SMI/E/12: Procedure for Dimming of Light in Vande Bharat Coaches
section: VB/SMI/E/12: Procedure for Dimming of Light in Vande Bharat Coaches
text: **Operation of Direct Light in Coach Level:** 1. Normally the local control switch for “DIRECT LIGHT” shall be kept always in AUTO mode so that the compartment lights can be switched ON/OFF from driver desk. 2. During 50% light selection from driver desk, only IDL is ON in compartment i.e. lights in dimming mode. If light is not sufficient to serve the food, the pantry staff can switch ON Direct Light in any of the coaches, by operating “DIRECT LIGHT” switch in that coach to MANUAL position. 3. As soon as completion of catering service the “DIRECT LIGHT” switch shall be kept in AUTO mode. 4. It is important to note that the local control switch for “DIRECT LIGHT” should be kept in AUTO mode whenever direct light is not required so that the direct light can be centrally switched ON/OFF from driver desk. **Labels on Panel:** *   AUTO *   MAN *   DIRECT LIGHT *   MEDHA

Railway Board Sub: Instruction on Summer preparedness drive for Vande Bharat train sets rakes These instructions are being issued for undertaking essential precautions and special drive to check all Vande Bharat trains prior to the commencement of summer season, so that typical failures attributed to high temperature do not occur and the desired level of reliability is maintained. A. Ventilation for Passenger and Crew: 1. Working of Cab AC in both driving and non-driving cabs and all RMPUs to be ensured before allowing the rake for service. 2. The bellows on RMPU connecting the shell structure with RMPU shall be checked for any sealant cracks, openings and shall be attended 3. Drain arrangement inside RMPU to be checked for any blockage for proper draining of condensate water 4. To ensure cleaning of HVAC filter at scheduled interval. 5. Inside the saloon, probable areas of sweating on the Air conditioning ducts shall be checked for any insulation damages.

text: 5. Inside the saloon, probable areas of sweating on the Air conditioning ducts shall be checked for any insulation damages. Loose clamping of west flex on flexible ducts shall be attended to avoid any leakage of conditioned air and subsequent condensation. Implementation of all the ICF CAI for sealing of unwanted openings shall be ensured. 6. Operation of RMPU with manual mode shall be avoided, to avoid excess cooling and subsequent condensation. 7. text: The jumper lead cables provide a low profile, low maintenance and high flex life solution for roof-line high voltage cables. The combination of industry-leading Raychem high voltage insulation materials and an engineering plastic strength member gives a design that is highly flexible over a wide temperature range and is resistant to the rigors of the high voltage rail environment.  25 kV roof-line inter-car jumper cables optimized for use in the rail environment.  Insulated to reduce the risk of flashover.  Low profile giving improved clearances and minimizing wind resistance.  Coiled form allows large flexing range with minimum space usage.  Flexible across a wide operating temperature range.  Dimensions customizable for individual applications.  Impact resistant.  Low weight.

title: VB/SMI/E/17: Cycle Check Inspection of Jumper Cables in Vande Bharat Trainset (incl. TE Connectivity HVJL manual)
text: The jumper boots provide a low maintenance solution for roof-line high voltage cables to reduce electrical clearance requirements and risk of flashover to the bolted high voltage connections from accidental contact with extraneous objects, e.g. birds or tree branches. The solution is highly flexible over a wide temperature range and is resistant to the rigors of the high voltage rail environment.  Roof-line jumper boots optimized for use in the rail environment.  Reduce electrical clearance requirements.  Reduce risk of flashover.  Reduce risk of metal part corrosion.  Reduce risk of short circuit during an accidental contact with a flying object.  Flexible across a wide operating temperature range.  Impact resistant.  Low weight. 6 of 26

text: CAUTION: 1. Over-torque (110% of Max. torque range) could cause breakage or lose accuracy. 2. Do not shake violently or drop wrench. 3. Do not use this wrench as a hammer. 4. Do not leave this wrench in any place exposed to excessive heat, humidity, or direct sunlight. 5. Do not use this apparatus in water.(not waterproof) 6. If the wrench gets wet, wipe it with a dry towel as soon as possible. The salt in seawater can be especially damaging. 7. Do not use organic solvents, such as alcohol or paint thinner when cleaning the wrench. 8. Keep this wrench away from magnets. 9. Do not expose this wrench to dust or sand as this could cause serious damage. 10. Do not apply excessive force to the LCD panel. 11. Apply torque slowly and graspe the center of the handle. Do not apply load to the end of handle. 12. When checking the accuracy or calibration, please use the bit head packed inside the blow mold case. (BM/BP series) BATTERY MAINTENANCE 1. When the wrench is not used for an extended period of time, remove the battery. 2. Keep a spare battery on hand when going on a long trip or to cold areas. 3. title: Implementation of CPA in Vande Bharat Trainset Rakes — Removal of VCD Foot Operated Switch
section: Implementation of CPA in Vande Bharat Trainset Rakes — Removal of VCD Foot Operated Switch
text: Office of CDE/Elec. Sub:  Implementation of CPA in Vande Bharat Train set rakes regarding removal of VCD foot (iii) ICF lt no MD/D/TrainSet/168/RBContract/186G dt.22.03.2025. RDSO vide letter under reference (i) has directed to carry out modifications in driver desk to deactivate the vigilance foot operated VCD switch provided for acknowledgement of VCD, which is located below the driver desk in all variants of Vande Bharat Train set rakes (Chair car, sleeper) to eliminate the possibility of rhythmic operation during momentarily micro sleep of driver for safety point of view during operation. It is further advised by RDSO that Resetting logic through other existing means shall continue to be same. The necessary modification which has to be carried out in driver desk by M/s.Medha for deactivation of foot operated VCD switch is hereby attached as Annexure-A. Further ICF vide letter under reference (iii) has suggested few improvement points to be carried out by M/s.Medha for the above modification for the deactivation of Vigilance foot operated VCD switch in driver desk (enclosed) , the same shall be ensured by user railways.

Sub: Failure of Vande Bharat Express due to Master Controller Malfunctioning – Maintenance Instructions Ref:   Preliminary Investigation report of NR on failure of T. No. 22426 (Rake ICF-9) dated 14 Jan 25 Based on preliminary investigation study by ICF, OEM (Schaultbau) and Medha at ICF (Report is enclosed as Annexure-A), following preventive/corrective action is suggested: During removal and re-fixing of Master Controller (MCH) cover in SS-1/SS-2 schedule, condition of insulation papers pasted inside the MCH cover shall be checked and replaced if found damaged. Medha has been advised to carry out one cyclic check of the master controller in the entire fleet and attend / replace any damaged insulation. The rakes which have undergone SS1 or SS2 will be checked on priority. Meanwhile OEM is working on re-design of MCH cover. All the existing covers will be replaced by modified cover on priority. Digitally signed by PRAVIN KUMAR

Please Detention of VB Express 22426 on 12 Jan 25 at ALJN due to Master Controller Malfunctioning It is mentioned in the preliminary investigation report by Sr.DME/TSD/SSB, that Train no- 22426, departed from ANVT to AYC at its scheduled time of 06:10 hrs with leading DTC 235080. At ALJN, loss of traction was experienced due to CCU breaker tripping.

title: Failure of Vande Bharat Express due to Master Controller Malfunctioning (ICF-9)
section: Failure of Vande Bharat Express due to Master Controller Malfunctioning (ICF-9)
text: 1. CCU breaker was reset by on board technical team, but traction not got enabled. 2. Emergency brake loop was found triggered without any command. 3. Traction selector loop was changed from position 1 to position2 but still issue persisted. (b) As per Medha recommendations: 4. BN recycling done by on board team, but still issue persisted. 5. Performed DIO/CCU testing, which revealed that BU1 on Forward Line No.10 was showing" OFF", resulting in a restriction in traction. Hence master controller of 235080 was replaced with master controller of 235081 at ALJN, and the train departs with 90 mins detention. (c) Investigation at SSB: It was found that One of the snap switches meant for direction selections, on the Master Controller was found to have shorted at connections due to cover insulation and less gap between cover and switch terminal. Due to this, the snap switch was not in the functioning properly. B. Investigation at ICF: Based on the above report, detailed study on new supplied MCH was made at ICF on

text: 1. To avoid recurrence of similar failure, Medha is advised to carry out one cyclic check of the master controller in the entire fleet and attend / replace any damaged insulation. The rakes which have undergone SS1 or SS2 to be checked on priority. Zonal railways are requested to kindly NOTE and coordinate with Medha for the same. 2. text: No. ICF/QMS/MDM/File/F015 Office of the GM/ Mech. Designs Date: 12.01.2024 A- Modifications shall be implemented immediately by user Rlys. B- Modifications shall be implemented by user Rlys as and when convenient There is a regular request from IRCTC for providing Parking space for Serving Trolley so as to improve the Food Serving experience for Passengers and also to avoid congestion near the IC doors. Accordingly ICF has implemented the provision in the New Vande Bharat Trainsets to be turned out from January,2024. As there is a need to implement this in the existing trainsets, the modifications required to be carried out are given in this CAI. Zonal Railways based on the requirement may implement this at the earliest. The framework of existing and modified Pantry storage are given in next page.

text: EXISTING LAYOUT SECTION-BB RAIL LEVEL 8 555 360 880 MODIFIED LAYOUT SECTION-BB RAIL LEVEL 8 555 360 880 150 210 13 JSL JINDAL STAINLESS Novacel PRE FILTER INCLUDED Instructions for provision of pre-filter for hot water boiler. ICF Drawing No. 890-6-4-002, Alt – ‘e’ 1. Item – 1 to 12, No Change 2. Item – 13 (10 inch high density spun pre-filter (5 Micron PP Spun) with housing compatible for all water purifiers size 3/8” pack of 1 of reputed make such as Eureka Forbes Aqua Guard or similar) to be procured Objective: To prevent scale formation in the boiler and also to ensure clear water from the boiler. Tools required: 1. Pneumatic Drilling machine 2. Screw driver 3. Plumbing tools Items required: 1. Suitable Reducers 2. Hose pipe 3. Teflon tape 4. Isolation cock Steps to be followed: 1. Remove the front cover of the sink module. 2. Connect the isolation cock outlet and pre filter inlet using suitable reducers. 3. Use Teflon tapes for all joints to avoid leakage. 4. Mount the pre-filter isolation cock assembly below the sink on the two channels with fasteners supplied along with the filter. 5.

title: ICF Coach Alteration Instruction A-2025/03: Nosecone sealing work in DTC of Vande Bharat
text: The objective of this work instruction is to describe the procedure to be followed in providing sealing on nosecone of DTC in Vande Bharat, in order to prevent ingress/egress of air. The following material/ consumables are required for carrying out sealing of nosecone, from outside, per rake. 1. Thermal insulation (polyolefin) foam of thickness 25mm – 6 Nos 2. Adhesive sealant to paste the foam with structure & FRP- 4L 3. 3M extreme sealant (1mm thick) tape-2 nos (4411W+, WHITE) 4. Closing sheet (Aluminium/SS)  to Drg. No.AAJ10033- 2 Nos 5. Closing sheet (Aluminium/SS)  to Drg. No.AAJ10107 -  2 Nos 6. Closing cover (Aluminium/SS)  to Drg No- AAJ10101- 2 Nos 7. Closing cover (Aluminium/SS)  to Drg No- AAJ10171- 2 Nos 8. Angle (Aluminium/SS)  to Drg No- AAJ10100- 2 Nos 9. Angle (Aluminium/SS)   to Drg No- AAJ10106- 2 Nos 10. Side closing sheet (Aluminium/SS)   to Drg No- AAJ10172- 4 Nos 11. Hexagon screw M6– 40 Nos 12. Spring lock washer B6- 40 Nos 13. Plain washer B6- 40Nos 14. Hexagon nut M6-40 Nos 15. 3M fire barrier rated foam FIP 1-Step- - 8 nos of 380ml 16. 3M 94 Primer (500 ml)-2 Nos 17. ACP SHEET- (120x1700 mm approx)-4 Nos 18.

text: 11. Detail procedure for the modifications: 1. Objective: To facilitate access to the VCB equipment for periodic maintenance by installing VCB Hatch Doors in coaches where pre-cut openings in the FRP ceiling panel are not available. This instruction mandates cut-away operations followed by fixing of hatch door as per the reference drawings. 2. Material/Consumables required As per the drawings in table-1. 3. Tools required 1. Measuring tape and marking tools. 2. Spirit Level- To ensure proper alignment of door frame. 3. Portable Hand Drill / Drill Machine(preferably battery operated, if power supply/pneumatic supply is not available nearby)- For drilling holes for fixing hatch frame 4. Center Punch & Hammer- For precise hole marking before drilling. 5. Pop riveting gun (preferably battery operated, if power supply/pneumatic supply is not available nearby). 6. Torque Wrench / Nut Driver Set- For tightening fasteners to specified torque. 7. Disc cutter (preferably battery operated, if power supply/pneumatic supply is not available nearby) - For cutting FRP panel as per required cut-out. 8. Deburring Tool / File Set- To smoothen cut edges of FRP after cutting 9.

title: ICF Coach Alteration Instruction B-2025/14: Modified Supply and Return Air Ducts (uniform cross section) (Vande Bharat)
section: ICF Coach Alteration Instruction B-2025/14: Modified Supply and Return Air Ducts (uniform cross section) (Vande Bharat)
text: ANNEXURE TRAINSET- AK WORK INSTRUCTION FOR REPLACEMENT OF EXISTING AIR DUCTS WITH MODIFIED WIDER AC DUCTS HAVING UNIFORM CROSS SECTION FOR VANDE BHARAT TRAINSET 1. Purpose & Scope This procedure defines the method to remove existing non-uniform cross sectional air ducts and replace them with modified ducts of uniform cross section, along with modified return air ducts, in Vande Bharat trainsets. The objective is to improve airflow distribution, enhance cooling efficiency, and reduce airflow imbalance issues. 2. Applicability This procedure applies to all coaches of Vande Bharat trainsets requiring air duct modification as per revised design. 3. Safety & Preparations 1. Isolate electrical supply to RMPUs and related controls before beginning the work. 2. Wear required PPE: safety shoes, gloves, safety goggles, and dust masks/respirators, as applicable. 3. Seats are to be covered adequately with plastic sheets/cloths to avoid damage 4. Use ladders with fall protection when working on roof ceiling. 5. Provide adequate ventilation in the coach during duct replacement. 4. Tools, Equipment & Materials 1. Tools/Equipment: a. Power screwdrivers, spanners, torque wrench b.

title: ICF Coach Alteration Instruction B-2025/14: Modified Supply and Return Air Ducts (uniform cross section) (Vande Bharat)
section: ICF Coach Alteration Instruction B-2025/14: Modified Supply and Return Air Ducts (uniform cross section) (Vande Bharat)
text: 4. Tools, Equipment & Materials 1. Tools/Equipment: a. Power screwdrivers, spanners, torque wrench b. Rivet gun/pop riveting tools c. Sealant applicator gun d. Measuring tape, spirit level, laser level e. Duct lifting/handling equipment f. Vacuum cleaner/air blower for duct cleaning 2. Materials: a. Modified supply air ducts (uniform cross section) as per ICF drawing b. Modified return air ducts c. Flexible duct connectors, clamps, insulation material, aluminium tape etc d. Silicon based sealant (Sikaflex) e. Fasteners, rivets, and brackets as per drawing 5. Procedure Step 1 – Documentation Record coach details, RMPU serial numbers, and duct identification. Photograph and document electrical connections, panels position with proper identification and duct routing for reference during installation. Step 2 – Removal of old supply and return air ducts Disconnect electrical connections in roof panels. Remove diffusers bottom profile and roof centre ceiling panels at duct locations. Disconnect the flexible connectors between the main duct and branch ducts. Remove diffuser top profile which comes with branch ducts.

title: ICF Coach Alteration Instruction B-2025/14: Modified Supply and Return Air Ducts (uniform cross section) (Vande Bharat)
section: ICF Coach Alteration Instruction B-2025/14: Modified Supply and Return Air Ducts (uniform cross section) (Vande Bharat)
text: Disconnect the flexible connectors between the main duct and branch ducts. Remove diffuser top profile which comes with branch ducts. Dismantle the existing main ducts systematically, starting from the RMPU side to the centre duct. Remove the existing return air ducts as well. Collect and segregate all removed materials for disposal in line with depot procedures. Page | 1

title: ICF Coach Alteration Instruction B-2025/14: Modified Supply and Return Air Ducts (uniform cross section) (Vande Bharat)
section: ICF Coach Alteration Instruction B-2025/14: Modified Supply and Return Air Ducts (uniform cross section) (Vande Bharat)
text: Step 3 – Preparation of Installation Area Clean mounting areas and remove residual sealant, dirt, and debris. Inspect duct supports, hangers, and brackets; replace parts that are corroded or damaged. Verify alignment points for the installation of new ducts. Remove cross brace arrangement to load modified wider AC duct as advised in ICF Drg No. (329) ICF/SK3-4-4-064. Step 4 – Installation of Modified Return Air Ducts Position the modified return air ducts in place of the old ones. Ensure proper fitment with the RMPU return air plenum. Secure the ducts using fasteners, rivets, and brackets, and seal all joints with silicon based sealant (Sikaflex). Step 5 – Installation of Modified Supply Air Ducts Position the modified uniform cross-sectional ducts as per the drawing. Align the ducts properly on the cross braces and support them temporarily with hangers. Connect branch duct connectors, ensuring a tight fit without gaps. Once alignment is verified, fix the ducts permanently using fasteners or rivets at specified intervals. Seal all joints using silicon based sealant (Sikaflex) and aluminium tape. Reinstall the flexible duct connectors between the main and branch ducts.

title: ICF Coach Alteration Instruction B-2025/14: Modified Supply and Return Air Ducts (uniform cross section) (Vande Bharat)
section: ICF Coach Alteration Instruction B-2025/14: Modified Supply and Return Air Ducts (uniform cross section) (Vande Bharat)
text: Seal all joints using silicon based sealant (Sikaflex) and aluminium tape. Reinstall the flexible duct connectors between the main and branch ducts. Refit the cross brace arrangement as shown in ICF Drg No. (329) ICF/SK3-4-4-064. Step 6 – Reinstallation of Roof Panels & Electrical Connections Refit the roof ceiling panels securely. Restore all electrical connections that were disconnected during removal. Verify that cable routing is correct and does not foul with the ducts. Step 7 – Testing & Verification Switch on both RMPUs. Measure air velocity at diffuser outlets and compare with baseline values. Check airflow near IC doors and verify uniform distribution. Conduct the return air flow measurements to confirm proper circulation. Record airflow velocity readings of complete coach for documentation. 6. Quality Checklist 1. Old ducts removed and disposed of properly 2. Modified supply air ducts installed as per drawing 3. Modified return air ducts installed as per drawing 4. All joints sealed with silicon based sealant 5. Fasteners/rivets provided as specified 6. Electrical connections restored correctly 7. Air velocity measured and recorded at diffuser outlets 16-10-2025 ICF/Chennai

text: The objective of this work instruction is to describe the procedure to be followed in providing sealing all around IC door periphery in Vande Bharat, in order to prevent ingress/egress of hot air. The following material/ consumables are required for carrying out sealing arrangement all around IC door periphery, per coach. 1. Adhesive sealant to paste the Bristles with Aluminum extrusions- 1 ltr 2. Material/Consumables required The following material/ consumables are required for carrying out replacement of upper trim panel. 1. title: ICF Coach Alteration Instruction B-2025/17: FRP Panel Rectification / Cleaning (Vande Bharat)
section: ICF Coach Alteration Instruction B-2025/17: FRP Panel Rectification / Cleaning (Vande Bharat)
text: 1. Objective: To outline the standard procedure for correcting gel coat blister, crater de-lamination, flaking,visible fibers, cracks and inclusion on FRP (Fiber Reinforced Plastic) panels. The primary approach is to restore the original color and gloss without painting. 2. Scope of work This SOP applies to all FRP parts or panels in  rework or maintenance operations that exhibit discoloration, yellowing, or dullness due to aging, UV exposure, or surface oxidation. The material used must comply with EN 45545 HL2 standard if fire retardance. 3. Definitions 1. FRP – Fiber Reinforced Plastic 2. Gel coat – A protective, colored surface layer of resin used in FRP panels 3. Oxidation – Surface damage or chalking due to UV and environmental exposure 4. 2K Clear Coat – Two-part protective clear coating (base + hardener) 4. Materials and Tools Required 5. Safety Instructions a. Always wear appropriate PPE (gloves, goggles, respirator mask). b. Ensure proper ventilation during solvent or paint application. c. Handle MEKP and chemicals as per manufacturer MSDS. d. Dispose of used materials appropriately. 6. Defects on the FRP panel’s surface. 6.1 Blister Page | 1

text: a) Step 1: Surface Cleaning: Wash the panel using a mild detergent and water. Rinse and let the surface dry completely. Degrease using isopropyl alcohol or acetone. b) Step 2: Gel coat with MEKP (100ml gel coat: 1ml MEKP) as per recommended is to be taken. c) Step 3: Prepare gel coat putty by adding chalk powder or aerosol powder to the above solution. d) Step 4: The surface where Gel coat to be applied must be dry and clean, before gel coat putty application. e) Step 5: The Gel coat putty prepared as above to be applied at the affected area, and wait for curing. f) Step 6: After curing, sanding operation to be done with 600 grit & 800 grit emery. g) Step7: Subsequently, finishing anti graffiti coating to be applied and wait for curing. h) Inspection to be carried out.
